Sandbox_ProjectALife.PresetWorld_tooltip: IF THE GAME STUTTERS, TURN THIS DOWN FIRST. Everything this mod costs in frame time comes from how many people the world is carrying, and this one setting decides that. The default is deliberately on the generous side so a new world feels inhabited; drop it one step and the county is still populated but noticeably cheaper. Rough guide on a mid-range machine: Deserted and Sparse are close to free, Balanced is the level everything is tested at, Crowded asks real work of a weaker CPU, and Insane is a stress test rather than a way to play. A dedicated server feels every step harder than singleplayer, because it simulates for everyone at once. One knob for every number below it. It sets how many survivors the world carries, how many towns are manned at the start, how often you meet them, whether they travel alone or in groups, how many outposts stand, when raids start and how far apart they are, and how large a raid wave, a scout party or a backup call is. Balanced is the tested default and writes nothing at all, so an existing save keeps every number it already has. Any option you set yourself still wins: the preset only moves options left at their own default, so tune one slider and the preset will not touch it -- the one thing it cannot see is you deliberately choosing the value that was already the default. Insane deliberately goes past the mod's own hard caps: up to 220 live hostiles (tested ceiling 120), 24 outposts (12), 4 per town (2), 12 outdoor camps (6), 40 offline squads (24), 4 task squads per outpost (2) and 8-strong scout parties (3). It is not tested at those numbers -- expect a heavier server, expect bugs, and back up your save first.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PresetWorld_option1: Deserted -- almost nobody left (lightest on FPS)
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PresetWorld_option2: Sparse -- a few lone survivors (light on FPS)
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PresetWorld_option3: Balanced -- the tested default, moderate FPS cost (no change)
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PresetWorld_option4: Crowded -- groups, outposts and frequent raids (heavy on FPS)
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PresetWorld_option5: Insane -- past the tested limits, unsupported (will cost frames)
Sandbox_ProjectALife.RealisticOutbreak_t: The first days of the outbreak, the way they would go. Police hold their stations and families their houses (towns are manned at the start unless you set that option yourself), the National Guard holds a checkpoint on the bridge north of West Point, and the first three days bring more of everything. After day 3 the police and the army are gone from the roads for good; the bridge checkpoint is abandoned after 72 hours and everything it placed is removed. On by default.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PersistentSquadCap_: Maximum squads carried between sessions, default 3. This does not limit new offline squads during the current session. Other crews last this server session. Outpost structures are saved separately. Lowering the limit retires excess saved squads on next load, not in front of players.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostTaskSquadCap: Simultaneous patrol, scavenging or hunting teams from each outpost. Default 1; zero disables dispatches. Crews are session-only; the site remains saved.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Party_LoneWeight_to: Relative frequency of natural 1–3-person parties. Faction overrides take priority.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Party_GroupWeight_t: Relative frequency of natural 4+ person groups. Default is one group for every three lone parties.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Offline_FoundGapHou: Minimum time between new offline parties, default 1.5; the offline squad cap still applies.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_Enabled_toolti: Automatic raids require a successfully spawned enemy scout party, buildup time, and the minimum day. The admin panel can force a raid.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_MinDay_tooltip: Automatic raids cannot begin before this world-age day.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_CooldownDays_t: Minimum time between automatic full-scale raids.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_Chance_tooltip: Chance to start the scout-led buildup on each check (every 10 game minutes by default). The default 0.02 with a 14-day cooldown means about one full-scale raid every six or seven weeks. 0 turns automatic raids off.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_CheckMinutes_t: How often the raid director checks automatic eligibility.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_Waves_tooltip: Number of attacking waves per raid.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_GroupSize_tool: Requested attackers in each wave. Spawn admission still enforces runtime limits.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_WaveDelayMinut: Paces reinforcement waves after the initial warning.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_Helicopter_too: Every A-Life helicopter: raid and reinforcement drops, night searchlights and flyovers. Off means none of them fly.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_ScoutBuildupHo: Wait this long after scouts successfully arrive before a raid can start.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_ScoutLifetimeH: An expired scout report cannot authorize a raid; new scouts must be sent.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Raid_ScoutSize_tool: Number of enemy scouts sent before an automatic full-scale raid.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_Chance_tool: Chance of a permitted support call succeeding.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_CooldownHou: Minimum game time between successful calls by the same group.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_GroupSize_t: Fallback when the caller/faction has no authored support size.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_MaxCalls_to: Limits repeated reinforcement requests from one group.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_SpotlightCh: Chance for an authorized helicopter spotlight call. Ground-only callers cannot use it.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_SpotlightSe: Follows the target player while outdoors; goes dark indoors.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_HelicopterS: Duration of the virtual support helicopter presentation.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Scavenge_BuildingRa: Maximum distance for selecting a nearby building; larger values increase search work.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Scavenge_CarryLimit: Maximum collected items before heading back to the camp/base depot.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Scavenge_ReturnAfte: Bring supplies home after searching this many buildings.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.ALifeEnabled_toolti: Off: no hostile factions spawn, and raids and outposts stop. Friendly, neutral and careful NPCs still spawn.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.NpcNight_tooltip: Flashlights: NPCs carry a light and see 12 tiles in the dark (20 with the light on you). Night vision: NPCs simply see at night; give them the goggles yourself.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.NightActivity_toolt: How likely a squad is to keep moving and working after dark. The rest find a house for the night or make a camp: they draw the curtains, hang sheets over the windows, sit tight until morning and leave the dead outside alone. No risks: everybody holes up. Risk takers: hardly anybody does.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OfflineSquadCap_too: Maximum offline roaming squads during a session, default 6. 0 turns the offline world off; nearby session encounters and saved outpost sites remain. The separate Saved squad limit controls how many return next session, without preventing new squads from founding now.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OfflineTickSeconds_: How often offline squads move and decide.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OfflineTravelTilesP: How far an offline squad walks in one in-game hour. Default 150, a walking pace at the default day length; towns are 1700-3400 tiles apart.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OfflineRevenge_tool: A squad that lost people to you and got away comes back for you two to three days later, with backup.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsEnabled_too: Fortified stations, held houses and forest camps appear over time, manned by a garrison that never leaves.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsMaxSites_to: How many outposts may stand at the same time. 0 turns them off.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsPerCity_too: How many outposts one town may hold.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsInterval_to: How often the world rolls for a new outpost, in game minutes (sleeping and fast-forward roll too). A world whose clock stands still falls back to the same number of real minutes.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsChance_tool: The chance each roll founds a new outpost.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsBuildRadius: A proposed outpost is built only while a player is this close (so the ground is loaded), and never within 40 tiles of anyone.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsSpawnRadius: A built outpost is manned when a player comes this close.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.SupportEnabled_tool: A squad in contact may call a quick-reaction squad; limited calls, a cooldown, and a real chance of no answer.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PopulationRate_tool: Scales the global encounter gate. 100 is the balanced default.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.GroupScale_tooltip: Scales natural group sizes. 100 keeps the authored sizes.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.SimulationRadius_to: Distance in tiles at which persistent actors receive physical shells.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.MaxHostiles_tooltip: Hard cap for natural persistent hostile actors.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterChance_too: Chance per roll for both natural spawners: the faction director rolls once per encounter check interval, the encounter director once per encounter roll interval. Default 25.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterInterval_t: Game hours between natural hostile encounter checks.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.SafehouseMargin_too: Extra no-spawn tiles around multiplayer safehouses.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Warfare_tooltip: Allows hostile A-Life factions to fight one another.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Scavenging_tooltip: Hostile looters may take nearby supplies.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Investigate_tooltip: Hostiles walk toward gunfire, shouts and other traces they notice.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Regroup_tooltip: Members that fall behind close back up on their group instead of drifting.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.GroupMarch_tooltip: Groups travel together in formation rather than as separate walkers.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.WeaponDrops_tooltip: Eligible NPC weapons may survive into corpse inventory.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.DropsWeaponChance_t: How often a dead NPC's gun or melee weapon stays on the body. Per NPC profile keeps each profile's own chance from the Creator. Anything else is the chance for every NPC. A spawn from the admin spawner still uses its own row. Needs Allow weapon drops on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.DropsWeaponConditio: What shape a dropped weapon is in. Per NPC profile keeps each profile's own rating and the early-game curve, where the first weeks mostly give you broken or nearly broken guns. Anything else is the condition of every dropped weapon, from every NPC. Broken means it has to be repaired before it works. The NPC still fights with it at full strength.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.WeaponJamming_toolt: Non-revolver NPC firearms can fail to fire, click, then be visibly racked clear.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.WeaponJamChance_too: Base chance per trigger pull for a non-revolver NPC firearm to jam. Zero disables jams even if the feature is enabled.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.BreachStrength_tool: How hard NPCs work a door, a window or a barricade when they break in. 100 is the tested default: a window takes three swings, a plank four, a plain door about half a minute, and only one man swings while the rest cover him. Lower it and they take longer; raise it and they come through faster.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.MultiHit_tooltip: A two-handed swing by an NPC carries into a second zombie standing in the arc, at three quarters of the blow. Zombies only, never people. Off by default.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.BulletPenetration_t: A round an NPC puts into a zombie goes on into the zombie standing right behind it (up to three squares). Zombies only, never people; better against a horde. Off by default.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PopulateOnStart_too: Once per world, the towns' rooms are read and a share of the places a survivor would hold -- police stations, fire houses, clinics and the dentist, gun stores, warehouses, gas stations, motels, diners, churches, schools, stores and houses -- are marked to be manned: Rare 10%%, Uncommon 20%%, Common 35%% of them, every town at least two. A marked place gets its residents the first time a player comes near, from a faction that fits the room: police in the station, the fire department in the fire house, hospital staff on the ward, a family in a house. They are persistent and saved with the world.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PopulateMax_tooltip: The most places in the whole world that Populate places on start may man. The heaviest places (stations, fire houses, clinics) are kept first.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Search_tooltip: NPCs walk to where a target was last seen and sweep the area before giving up.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.SearchShout_tooltip: Shouting draws every NPC within earshot toward you.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.SearchCallout_toolt: An NPC that spots something tells its group where, once. Not a live feed.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Clues_tooltip: With nothing to fight, NPCs search areas where they notice signs of survivors.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesVehicles_toolt: A running or hotwired vehicle marks the area around it as worth searching.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesBarricades_too: Planked windows and doors mark a building as somebody's.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesPlayerBuilt_to: Player-built walls, gates and fences mark a location as occupied.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesPower_tooltip: An active generator is strong evidence somebody is living nearby.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.CluesWeight_tooltip: Scales how readily NPCs act on traces. Higher investigates weaker evidence; lower needs a stronger lead.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Voice_tooltip: Plays recorded voice clips for what NPCs say. Off by default: NPCs talk in text only. Pain and death sounds are not affected.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.ShowAdminTools: Show admin tools in the right-click menu
Sandbox_ProjectALife.ShowAdminTools_tool: The spawn panel, encounter list, outpost builder and raid setup. Turn this off for a clean right-click menu; Runtime status and the Creator stay either way. Admins on a server are unaffected.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.VehicleDamage_toolt: A moving vehicle hurts an NPC it hits, scaled by speed. Turn this off to stop the vehicle check running at all. NPCs still cannot reach you through an intact car window either way.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.AimDifficulty_toolt: How often NPC gunfire hits players. Medium is each NPC's own aiming skill, unchanged. Very Easy is 40%% of it, Easy 65%%, Hard 125%%, Very Hard 150%%, Hardcore 180%%. Accuracy against zombies is set on the Combat page.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.AimZombiePercent_to: Scales how often NPC gunfire hits a ZOMBIE. 100 is unchanged; raise it if crews look helpless against a horde. Does not affect their aim against you.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Tracers_tooltip: Draws a visible streak along each shot an NPC fires. Muzzle flash, gunfire and casings are unaffected either way.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleCover_tooltip: Armed NPCs get out of the line of fire to reload, break contact when hurt, and fight from behind walls and corners.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleWithdraw_tool: A shooter that is losing breaks contact, runs about a block back, holes up out of sight -- inside a building when there is one -- then comes back in from another side. Ranged only; melee always closes.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleHealing_toolt: After a fight, a wounded NPC stops, bandages, and loses the limp and the bleeding.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Wounds_tooltip: Hits mark NPCs: a leg wound takes their run away, and below ten percent health they bleed out in seconds unless they bandage.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.SprintEnabled_toolt: Allows sprint windows for melee closing, cover moves, and retreats. Off keeps those moves at a run or walk.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleGunner_toolti: A shooter that loses sight of its target dumps the magazine into the last known position, full auto, spraying left and right. Pistols magdump too.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Encounters_tooltip: The encounter director: patrols, raids, scavenging parties, assassination squads and garrisons rolled from the catalog near players, placed by the map's own town zones.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.EncounterRollInterv: Game minutes between encounter director rolls (sleeping and fast-forward roll too). Default 60, range 10-720. The spawn chance per roll comes from the encounter chance option.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.DormantTtl_tooltip: A parked NPC nobody has been near for this many in-game hours is cleaned up. Persistent NPCs (admin anchors, encounter garrisons) never expire. 0 disables the cleanup.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleBehaviors_too: The conduct layer: squad leaders that deploy and rally their group, snipers that keep distance, medics that dress their wounded, ambushers that wait in the dark, stealth killers. Off disables every conduct at once.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.ModuleStrafe_toolti: Armed NPCs keep the gun on their target, or on where it was last seen, while they walk, back off or sidestep.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.WorldMode_tooltip: Full: squads roam the whole map while nobody is near (offline simulation) and appear when you get close; outposts rise and fall on their own. Local only: no offline squads -- NPC groups exist only near players (cheapest); outposts still rise.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.WorldMode_option1: Full A-Life (offline squads roam the map)
Sandbox_ProjectALife.WorldMode_option2: Local only (groups near players; outposts stay)
Sandbox_ProjectALife.RateEncounters_tool: How often the encounter director rolls a new group near players. Low halves the chance, Abundant triples it (the roll interval is unchanged).
Sandbox_ProjectALife.RateGroups_tooltip: How many groups the world keeps: the spawn multiplier and the offline squad cap together. Low halves both, Abundant triples them (within their own ceilings).
Sandbox_ProjectALife.RateSurvivors_toolt: How often the factions that are friendly or neutral to the player are picked when a group is founded. Low halves their weight against the hostile ones, Abundant triples it.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.RateMetaEvents_tool: Distant gunfire, helicopters, car crashes and the world's ambience: Low halves the daily and weekly caps and doubles the gap between events, Abundant triples the caps and shortens the gap.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.OutpostsOutsideCity: Camps and field bases outside towns (max)
How many outdoor sites -- forest camps, field bases, aid stations, depots -- may stand at once, on top of the per-town limit for fortified buildings. 0 disables outdoor sites.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRestEnabled_t: Patrols and scout parties stop off the road every few hours and after a fight: a circle, one sits, one smokes, the rest drink and talk, then the route resumes.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRestMinMinute: The shortest rest, in game minutes.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRestMaxMinute: The longest rest, in game minutes.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRestEveryHour: Game hours between scheduled rests, per squad, with some jitter. A rest after a fight comes on its own.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkEnabled_tooltip: Type in chat near NPCs and they answer: questions, requests, threats, yes or no. They also react with words when you hit them or help them in a fight.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkSinglePlayerCha: Single player has no chat window. With this on, the Toggle chat key opens a small line to talk to NPCs. Start a line with ! to shout it.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkPresence_toolti: Friendly and neutral people stop and look at you when you come close and say something; friends passing by say a word; outlaw crews call out a stranger.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.TalkRiskAssessment_: Scared ordinary people do not open fire on someone who has not attacked them, and back off when they are badly outgunned. Veterans and predators never do.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.RobberyEnabled_tool: Outlaw crews may hold up a lone player instead of shooting: hands up, the weapon down, three or four valuable items taken, then they leave. Refuse, and they shoot.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.RobberyChance_toolt: Scales how often an outlaw crew chooses to rob instead of fighting. 100 is normal, 0 never, 200 twice as often.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.RadioKnoxCounty_too: A survivor-run station with scanner traffic, military chatter, call-ins, stories, jokes and rumours about what is really happening in your world.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.RadioKnoxFrequency_: Default 99600 = 99.6 MHz. Choose an unused FM frequency if the emergency station or another mod already occupies it. The station never replaces another channel. Restart the server after changing this; open a radio to add the matching preset.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Preset_World_toolti:
Sets every population and frequency option in this menu at once -- 23 of them. Anything you change by hand afterwards is kept, and the sliders below may still SHOW their old numbers even though the preset is in force. What each one means:

SPARSE - 12 hostiles, 2 outposts, encounters every 8h. A quiet county.
LOW - 20 hostiles, 4 outposts, encounters every 6h.
BALANCED - 32 hostiles, 6 outposts, encounters every 4h. The tested default; picking it writes nothing and leaves your own edits alone.
ABUNDANT - 56 hostiles, 9 outposts (2 per town), encounters every 3h, bigger raids.
INSANE - 220 hostiles, 24 outposts, encounters every 2h. A stress test, not a game: this load has never been validated in multiplayer.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Realistic_Outbreak_: Ties the mod to the world you started: the state falls away over the first week, and who you meet follows the calendar rather than a flat roll. Recommended: on for a normal start, off if you are testing.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.World_HostileEnable: The master switch. Off means no A-Life people at all -- the mod stays loaded and the admin tools still work. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Population_RatePerc: Scales how often you run into anybody, in percent. 100 is the tested rate; 200 is a busy county, 50 a quiet one. The single biggest performance dial in this menu. Recommended: 100.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Population_PartyPer: Scales how many people are in each group, in percent. 100 keeps the authored sizes -- a family is three, an army fireteam is five. Above 150 the fights get long. Recommended: 100.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.World_SimRadius_too: How far out, in tiles, people are fully simulated. Beyond it they are still there and still moving, just cheaply. Raising this is the second biggest cost in the menu. Recommended: 90; drop to 60 on a weak machine.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Population_HostileC: Hard ceiling on living hostile people at once. Nothing spawns past it, whatever else is set. Recommended: 32. A strong machine handles 48; 80+ is a stress test, not a game.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Encounters_RollPerc: Percent chance that an encounter is rolled when the interval comes round. Recommended: 25.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Encounters_GapHours: Game hours between encounter rolls. Lower means more often. Recommended: 4.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.World_SafehouseClea: Tiles of clearance kept around a safehouse -- nothing spawns inside it. Raise it if people appear too close to your base. Recommended: 8.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.World_FactionWarfar: Factions fight each other, not only you. Turning this off makes the county quieter and cheaper, and removes most of what you will watch happen from a distance. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Behavior_Retreat_to: People who are losing break and run instead of dying in place. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Behavior_Scavenge_t: Crews can stop you, search you and take what you are carrying. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Behavior_Investigat: Gunshots and shouting are investigated. Off makes people deaf to everything but line of sight. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Behavior_Regroup_to: A scattered group re-forms on its leader instead of fighting alone. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Behavior_MarchToget: Groups travel together rather than trickling in one at a time. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Drops_WeaponsEnable: Bodies drop the weapon they were carrying. Condition follows the calendar: week one is scrap, a month in it is worth taking. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Combat_JamChance_to: Percent chance per shot. 1.0 is roughly one jam per magazine and a half. Above 5 the fights read as comedy. Recommended: 1.0.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Breach_Strength_too: How hard people hit doors and barricades, as a percent of normal. 200 means a locked door is no obstacle. Recommended: 100.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Combat_MultiHit_too: One swing can hit more than one target. Recommended: off -- it makes crowds melt.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Combat_BulletPenetr: Rounds pass through a body into whatever is behind it. Recommended: off unless you want friendly fire to matter a lot.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Combat_Wounds_toolt: Hits leave lasting wounds -- limps, bleeding, an arm that stops working. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Combat_VisibleTrace: Draws a visible tracer for every shot. Useful for watching a firefight you are not in; not realistic. Recommended: off.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Population_Populate: Puts people into towns before you ever get there, so a place you walk into is already occupied. EXPERIMENTAL and costly on a cold start. Recommended: off for your first world.
How many places may be pre-populated. Only matters when the option above is on. Recommended: 30.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Population_DormantT: Game hours a person is remembered after you leave the area. They come back the same person rather than a new stranger. 0 forgets immediately. Recommended: 8.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Search_Enabled_tool: People search bodies and containers after a fight instead of standing over them. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Search_ShoutRespons: Shouting is heard and answered. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Search_GroupCallout: Groups call to each other -- contact reports, warnings, names. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Clues_Enabled_toolt: People read the world for signs of you: a parked car, a barricade, a lit window. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Clues_Vehicles_tool: A vehicle left somewhere is a sign somebody is nearby. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Clues_Barricades_to: Boarded windows say the place is held. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Clues_PlayerBuilt_t: Walls and floors you built are read as yours. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Clues_Power_tooltip: A generator running is the loudest sign there is. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Clues_WeightMultipl: How heavily clues pull attention toward your base. Above 2.0 you will be found often. Recommended: 1.0.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Voice_Enabled_toolt: Spoken lines. Off leaves the text only. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_Enabled_toolti: People talk -- warnings, demands, contact calls. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_SinglePlayerCh: Shows their lines in the chat box in single player as well as over their heads. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_Presence_toolt: They comment on what they can see of you -- what you are holding, whether you are bleeding. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Talk_RiskAssessment: They weigh you up out loud before deciding. This is what makes a stand-off feel like one. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Robbery_Enabled_too: Crews can hold you up rather than simply shooting. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Robbery_Chance_tool: Percent weighting on how often a hold-up is chosen over an attack. 200 means they nearly always try to rob first. Recommended: 100.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Radio_KnoxCounty_to: The county broadcast: reports, rumours, the occasional idiot with a transmitter. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Radio_KnoxFrequency: The frequency to tune a radio to, in kHz. Recommended: 99600.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Modules_Behaviors_t: The behaviour modules as a set -- cover, flanking, resting, scavenging and the rest. Off leaves people able to walk and shoot and nothing else. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Modules_Cover_toolt: They use cover instead of standing in the open. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Modules_Withdraw_to: A losing group falls back in order rather than scattering. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Modules_Healing_too: They bandage themselves and each other between fights. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Modules_Sprint_tool: They can sprint. Off makes every chase winnable. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Modules_Gunner_tool: A designated gunman lays down covering fire while the others move. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Modules_Strafe_tool: They move while shooting rather than rooting in place. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Encounters_Enabled_: Roadside set-pieces: roadblocks, ambushes, rooftop shooters, crashed cars. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Encounters_Interval: Real minutes between encounter attempts. Lower means a busier road. Recommended: 60.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Offline_SquadCap_to: How many groups travel the map while you are elsewhere. They are cheap -- they only cost anything when you meet one. Recommended: 6; raise to 12 for a crowded county.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Population_Persiste: How many groups are written into your save and survive a restart. Recommended: 3.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Outposts_TaskSquadC: How many squads a single outpost may have out on a job at once. Recommended: 1 -- an outpost calls for backup when attacked, so it does not need people standing about.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Offline_TickSeconds: Seconds between offline world updates. Higher is cheaper and coarser. Recommended: 20.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Offline_TravelTiles: How fast groups cross the map when you are not looking. 150 is a walking pace with stops. Recommended: 150.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Offline_RevengeEnab: A group that lost people to you comes back for you, days later, at where you were last seen. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Outposts_Enabled_to: Factions build and hold real places -- garrisons, patrols, watches, a radio. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Outposts_MaxSites_t: How many outposts exist at once. Each one is a standing population, so this is a real cost. Recommended: 6; 10 or more wants a strong machine.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Outposts_PerCity_to: How many outposts may sit around one town. Recommended: 1.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Outposts_OutsideCit: How many outposts may sit out in the country rather than near a town. Recommended: 2.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Outposts_IntervalMi: Real minutes between attempts to found a new outpost. Recommended: 30.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Outposts_Chance_too: Percent chance an attempt succeeds. Recommended: 20.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Outposts_BuildRadiu: How far from you, in tiles, an outpost may be built. Too small and you watch one appear. Recommended: 120.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Outposts_SpawnRadiu: How close you must be, in tiles, before an outpost puts its garrison in the world. Recommended: 90.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Support_Enabled_too: Groups can call for help -- a car pulling up, or a helicopter putting people on ropes. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Night_Sight_tooltip: What people do after dark. Flashlights is the readable choice; Hidden makes the nights genuinely dangerous. Recommended: Flashlights.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Night_Activity_tool: How much happens at night at all. Recommended: Moderate.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRest_Enabled_: Patrols stop, sit and rest instead of walking forever. Recommended: on.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRest_MinMinut: Shortest rest, in game minutes. Recommended: 20.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRest_MaxMinut: Longest rest, in game minutes. Recommended: 45.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.PatrolRest_EveryHou: Game hours of walking before a patrol wants a rest. Recommended: 3.0.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.World_Mode_tooltip: How the world is read for placement -- which towns and roads count. Recommended: leave as the preset set it.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Rate_Encounters_too: How often roadside set-pieces happen. Recommended: Normal.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Rate_Groups_tooltip: How often travelling groups appear. Recommended: Normal.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Rate_Survivors_tool: How often lone survivors appear. Recommended: Normal.
Sandbox_ProjectALife.Rate_MetaEvents_too: How often distant events happen -- gunfire over the hill, a helicopter, a crash. These are atmosphere and cost almost nothing. Recommended: Normal.
